post_r1_state_universe.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION
post_r1_state_universe.statement: post-R1 denotes any reachable state with r_count=1 from one of the five short roots (root_r_count=0). r2_predecessor_geometry.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION, fully verified against engine mutation code
r2_predecessor_geometry.monotonicity_fact: component_forest is built purely from orbit_masks bits (one union per set bit, orbit-node to hexagon-node of that visited port). orbit_masks bits are only ever SET, never cleared (`om[q] |= 1 << phase` in superperm_partial_f1.py line 245; the preceding guard actively forbids re-setting an already-set bit). Therefore the induced partition of {orbits} union {hexagons} into components can only COARSEN (merge, never split) along any walk; any two nodes in the same component at some point remain so forever.
r2_predecessor_geometry.practical_consequence: the first step at which R2's eventual source and target orbit become same-component is a well-defined, monotone event; the pilot's raw per-state orbit_masks (already part of state serialization, no extra decoration needed) is sufficient to compute it in post-processing
r2_predecessor_geometry.status: method for computing this metric is fully specified; empirical values are open

safe_prune_candidates.label: CLAUDE_PROPOSAL
safe_prune_candidates.statement: for any post-R1 (r_count==1) state reached from a short root, if Ndef(state) >= n_limit (3), no Target A boundary reachable from that state lies within the disclosed Area-A scope; the state and its subtree may be pruned, tightening N_exceeded_monotone's threshold by exactly 1 at r_count==1 states specifically

hand_proof.label: CLAUDE_HAND_PROOF
steps: 1. An R-kind edge has (dS,dF,dO)=(1,0,0) by its own joint_kind definition (3,False,False); by the already-proven identity dNdef=dS+dF-dO, dNdef=+1 exactly for any R-kind edge.

2. From a post-R1 state, Target A's recognizer requires the boundary to be exactly the second R (is_target_a_edge, r_count_before==1); no Z2/Z3 edge changes Ndef (dNdef=0 for both, Round 37 conservation table).

3. Therefore Ndef(boundary_child) = Ndef(current_state) + 1 EXACTLY for every Target A boundary reachable from a post-R1 state -- the same '+k exactly' argument the Round 37 envelope theorem already uses for Ndef(boundary)=Ndef(root)+k, specialized to k=1.

4. N_exceeded_monotone's own disclosed scope requires Ndef(boundary_child) <= n_limit. Substituting step 3: Ndef(current_state) <= n_limit - 1. Contrapositive: Ndef(current_state) >= n_limit certifies no Area-A-scope Target A boundary is reachable from that state.

safe_prune_candidates.exact_scope: r_count==1 states reached from a root with root_r_count==0 (the five short roots specifically); requires Area-A scope (n_limit=3) exactly as N_exceeded_monotone already requires; does not apply as stated to long-excursion roots (root_r_count=1 already)
safe_prune_candidates.required_decoration: r_count and Ndef, both already present in every existing frontier record -- no new field needed for this specific prune
safe_prune_candidates.honesty_check: for these five specific short roots, Ndef(root)=0 uniformly and only R-kind edges move Ndef, so post-R1 pre-R2 states have Ndef pinned at exactly 1 (well below the >=3 threshold). This candidate is expected to be correct but VACUOUS for the short-root family as currently scoped -- it would never actually fire here. Recorded anyway because (a) it documents a generally-applicable refinement other roots could use, and (b) its predicted vacuity is itself a checkable claim.
safe_prune_candidates.minimal_counterexample_search_request_fo: among all r_count==1 records the corrected pilot actually generates from the five short roots, report the distribution of Ndef. Expected: {1: <all of them>}. Any record with Ndef != 1 at r_count==1 is either evidence this prune is not vacuous (if Ndef>=3) or evidence of an engine/decoration bug (if Ndef is anything other than 0 or 1 in that population). This is a single aggregate histogram over data the pilot already produces, not a new search.

safe_prune_candidates.label: considered, NOT proposed as a prune
safe_prune_candidates.statement: the monotonicity fact under r2_predecessor_geometry is tempting to read as a prune ('not yet same-component => prune') but that direction is UNSOUND: components can still merge later via further Z2/Z3/R edges, so 'not yet same-component' is never a valid impossibility certificate -- exactly backwards from what a sound prune needs.
safe_prune_candidates.why_no_prune_proposed: no sound prune was found in the other direction either (a lower bound on how many further edges are needed to force a merge) without either running new code against live states (out of scope for this role) or asserting an unverified claim about specific hexagon/orbit adjacency structure. Per the assigning instruction ('only propose a new prune if you can provide a hand proof of soundness'), the correct response to an incomplete proof is not to propose it.
safe_prune_candidates.retained_value: the monotonicity fact itself is retained as a CLAUDE_OBSERVATION under r2_predecessor_geometry because it is still useful for correctly COMPUTING the metric, even though it yields no prune
